# pcfg: ported to Alea.jl from PluckArtifact.jl/src/table1/sequence_models/
# pluck/pcfg.jl of the artifact of Bowers et al., "Stochastic Lazy
# Knowledge Compilation for Inference in Discrete Probabilistic Programs"
# (PLDI 2025), Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15051140 (CC-BY-4.0): the Pluck
# program of the paper's Table 1, row PCFG. The query is the probability
# that the grammar
#   S  -> XX YY | YY XX     (by a flip 0.5)
#   XX -> a | b XX XX       (a by a flip 0.5)
#   YY -> c | c XX | c S    (c alone by a flip 0.5, then XX or S by another)
# generates TARGET from S. The artifact's Dice.jl baseline
# (sequence_models/dice/pcfg.jl) is another grammar (YY -> c XX by 0.5)
# and bounds its recursion by fuel; this port is Pluck's grammar, bounded
# by the target alone.
#
# The generation reads the target left to right: generates(sym, i, j)
# is that sym, generated at position i, is the target's symbols i to
# j - 1. Each choice is keyed by its symbol and its position, which gives
# the original's distribution where no derivation expands one symbol twice
# at one position. The grammar has neither left recursion nor an empty
# production: S's productions start with XX or YY, and XX's and YY's with
# a terminal, so a derivation expands at a position at most S and then one
# of XX and YY, each once. No generation then reads one key twice, a
# derivation has the original's probability, and the choices at its keys
# fix it, so that two derivations exclude each other.
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr

const TARGET = [:c, :b, :b, :b, :a, :b, :b, :a, :b, :a, :b, :b, :a, :b, :a, :a, :a, :a, :a, :b, :a, :a, :a]

function pcfg_generates(target)
    n = length(target)
    x_ends = [flip(0.5) for _ in 1:n]     # XX at i is a (otherwise b XX XX)
    s_order = [flip(0.5) for _ in 1:n]    # S at i is XX YY (otherwise YY XX)
    y_ends = [flip(0.5) for _ in 1:n]     # YY at i is c alone
    y_xx = [flip(0.5) for _ in 1:n]       # YY at i goes on with XX (otherwise S)
    memo = Dict{Tuple{Symbol, Int, Int}, AnyBool}()
    any_of(xs) = reduce(|, xs; init = false)
    function generates(sym, i, j)
        haskey(memo, (sym, i, j)) && return memo[(sym, i, j)]
        g = if i > n || j <= i
            false
        elseif sym == :XX
            a = target[i] == :a && j == i + 1 ? x_ends[i] : false
            b = target[i] == :b ? !x_ends[i] & any_of([generates(:XX, i + 1, k) & generates(:XX, k, j) for k in i+2:j-1]) : false
            a | b
        elseif sym == :YY
            if target[i] != :c
                false
            else
                alone = j == i + 1 ? y_ends[i] : false
                on = !y_ends[i] & ((y_xx[i] & generates(:XX, i + 1, j)) | (!y_xx[i] & generates(:S, i + 1, j)))
                alone | on
            end
        else
            xy = any_of([generates(:XX, i, k) & generates(:YY, k, j) for k in i+1:j-1])
            yx = any_of([generates(:YY, i, k) & generates(:XX, k, j) for k in i+1:j-1])
            (s_order[i] & xy) | (!s_order[i] & yx)
        end
        memo[(sym, i, j)] = g
    end
    generates(:S, 1, n + 1)
end

model() = @alea begin
    pcfg_generates(TARGET)
end

% sorted_list: ported to ProbLog from PluckArtifact.jl/src/table1/
% sequence_models/pluck/sorted_list.jl of the artifact of Bowers, Lew,
% Tenenbaum, Solar-Lezama and Mansinghka, "Stochastic Lazy Knowledge
% Compilation for Inference in Discrete Probabilistic Programs" (PLDI
% 2025), Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15051140 (CC-BY-4.0): the Pluck program of
% the paper's Table 1, row Sorted List. The query is the probability that
%   generate min = if flip 0.5 then Nil
%                  else let m = min + randnat in Cons m (generate m)
% with randnat geometric (0 by a flip 0.5, otherwise one more than
% randnat), generates [0, 3, 7, 12, 13, 15, 16, 20] from 0: 2^-37.
%
% The list is read against the target left to right: list(I, Min) holds
% where generate Min is the target from element I on, and step(I, K, D)
% where element I's randnat, at K, goes on to D. A choice is keyed by the
% element it draws and, in randnat, by its count, which gives the
% original's distribution where no generation reads one key twice. The
% elements are drawn once each, in order, and a randnat's count grows by
% one at each of its flips, so no generation reads one key twice, it has
% the original's probability, and the choices at its keys fix it, so that
% two generations exclude each other.
at(0, 0). at(1, 3). at(2, 7). at(3, 12). at(4, 13). at(5, 15). at(6, 16). at(7, 20).
elements(8).

0.5::ends(I) :- elements(N), between(0, N, I).
0.5::stops(I, K) :- at(I, V), between(0, V, K).

step(I, D, D) :- stops(I, D).
step(I, K, D) :- K < D, \+stops(I, K), K1 is K + 1, step(I, K1, D).
list(N, _) :- elements(N), ends(N).
list(I, Min) :- at(I, V), \+ends(I), V >= Min, D is V - Min, step(I, 0, D),
  I1 is I + 1, list(I1, V).

generated :- list(0, 0).
query(generated).

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; pluck_string_editing.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define in-facts (hash-ref db "in/2" (make-hash)))
(define input-facts (hash-ref db "input/1" (make-hash)))
(define out-facts (hash-ref db "out/2" (make-hash)))
(define target-facts (hash-ref db "target/1" (make-hash)))

(define in in-facts)

(define deleted (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.01::deleted(K) :- in(K,_A1).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs in)])
    (match-define (cons (list K _A1) x1) t2)
    (add! deleted (list K) (&& x1 (flip 0.01)))))

(define input input-facts)

(define place (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; place(K) :- input(N), between(0,N,K).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs input)])
    (match-define (cons (list N) x1) t2)
    (for ([K (in-range 0 (+ N 1))])
      (add! place (list K) x1))))

(define target target-facts)

function gen_sorted_nat(min_val, fuel)
    fuel == 0 && return min_val

    end

# sequence_models/pluck/string_editing.jl of the artifact of Bowers et al.,
# "Stochastic Lazy Knowledge Compilation for Inference in Discrete

# (CC-BY-4.0): the Pluck program of the paper's Table 1, row String
# Editing, with the perturb its benchmark defines (perturb_defs, "the one
# we're using"). The query is the probability that perturb turns INPUT
# into OUTPUT:
#   perturb Nil         = random_string 0.99
#   perturb (Cons c cs) = let delete = flip 0.01, insertion = random_string 0.99,
#                             rest = perturb cs
#                         in if delete then rest
#                            else insertion ++ Cons (if flip 0.01 then random_char else c) rest
#   random_string p     = if flip p then Nil else Cons random_char (random_string p)
# with random_char uniform over a to e. The artifact's Dice.jl baseline
# (sequence_models/dice/string_editing.jl) is another model and bounds
# its recursion by fuel; this port is Pluck's model, bounded by the two
# strings alone.
#
# The perturbation is read against OUTPUT left to right: perturbs(k, i)
# is that perturb of INPUT from position k is OUTPUT from position i to
# its end, and inserts(k, i, j) that the string inserted before input
# position k (k = length(INPUT) + 1: after the input) is OUTPUT's
# characters i to j - 1. A choice is keyed by the input position it
# perturbs and, within an inserted string, by the output position it
# writes, which gives the original's distribution where no perturbation
# reads one key twice. The input positions are perturbed once each, in
# order, and an inserted string writes each output position once, its end
# read at the position after its last character; an empty insertion, or a
# deleted input character, leaves the output position to the next input
# position, a key of its own. No perturbation then reads one key twice, it
# has the original's probability, and the choices at its keys fix it, so
# that two perturbations exclude each other.
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr

const INPUT = "edcc"
const OUTPUT = "eddde"

function string_editing_perturbs(input, output)
    n, m = length(input), length(output)
    code(c) = DistUInt{3}(c - 'a')
    random_char() = uniform(DistUInt{3}, 0, 5)
    deleted = [flip(0.01) for _ in 1:n]
    replaced = [flip(0.01) for _ in 1:n]
    replacement = [random_char() for _ in 1:n]
    ends = [flip(0.99) for _ in 1:n+1, _ in 1:m+1]
    inserted = [random_char() for _ in 1:n+1, _ in 1:m]
    any_of(xs) = reduce(|, xs; init = false)
    memo_ins = Dict{Tuple{Int, Int, Int}, AnyBool}()
    function inserts(k, i, j)
        haskey(memo_ins, (k, i, j)) && return memo_ins[(k, i, j)]
        g = if i == j
            ends[k, i]
        elseif i > m || j < i
            false
        else
            !ends[k, i] & prob_equals(inserted[k, i], code(output[i])) & inserts(k, i + 1, j)
        end
        memo_ins[(k, i, j)] = g
    end
    written(k, d) = (!replaced[k] & (input[k] == d)) | (replaced[k] & prob_equals(replacement[k], code(d)))
    memo = Dict{Tuple{Int, Int}, AnyBool}()
    function perturbs(k, i)

        end
        memo[(k, i)] = g
    end
    perturbs(1, 1)
end

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; pluck_pcfg.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define w-facts (hash-ref db "w/2" (make-hash)))
(define symbols-facts (hash-ref db "symbols/1" (make-hash)))

(define w w-facts)

(define s-order (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.5::s_order(I) :- w(I,_A1).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs w)])
    (match-define (cons (list I _A1) x1) t2)
    (add! s-order (list I) (&& x1 (flip 0.5)))))

(define x-ends (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.5::x_ends(I) :- w(I,_A1).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs w)])
    (match-define (cons (list I _A1) x1) t2)
    (add! x-ends (list I) (&& x1 (flip 0.5)))))

(define w-by-2 (index w 1))
;; x/2: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define (stage-x x)
  (define next-x (make-hash))
  (define x-by-1 (index x 0))
  ;; x(I,J) :- w(I,a), x_ends(I), J is I + 1.
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref w-by-2 (list 'a) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list I _) x1) t2)
    (let ([J (+ I 1)])
      (for ([x3 (in-list (probe x-ends (list I)))])
        (add! next-x (list I J) (&& x1 x3)))))
  ;; x(I,J) :- w(I,b), \+ x_ends(I), I1 is I + 1, x(I1,K), x(K,J).
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref w-by-2 (list 'b) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list I _) x1) t2)
    (let ([I1 (+ I 1)])
      (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref x-by-1 (list I1) null))])
        (match-define (cons (list _ K) x3) t4)
        (for ([t6 (in-list (hash-ref x-by-1 (list K) null))])
          (match-define (cons (list _ J) x5) t6)
          (add! next-x (list I J) (&& x1 (! (holds x-ends (list I))) x3 x5))))))
  (list next-x))
(define-values (x)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-x rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define y-ends (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.5::y_ends(I) :- w(I,_A1).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs w)])
    (match-define (cons (list I _A1) x1) t2)
    (add! y-ends (list I) (&& x1 (flip 0.5)))))

(define y-xx (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.5::y_xx(I) :- w(I,_A1).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs w)])
    (match-define (cons (list I _A1) x1) t2)
    (add! y-xx (list I) (&& x1 (flip 0.5)))))

(define x-by-1 (index x 0))
;; s/2, y/2: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define (stage-s s y)
  (define next-s (make-hash))
  (define next-y (make-hash))
  (define s-by-1 (index s 0))
  (define y-by-1 (index y 0))
  ;; y(I,J) :- w(I,c), y_ends(I), J is I + 1.
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref w-by-2 (list 'c) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list I _) x1) t2)
    (let ([J (+ I 1)])
      (for ([x3 (in-list (probe y-ends (list I)))])
        (add! next-y (list I J) (&& x1 x3)))))
  ;; y(I,J) :- w(I,c), \+ y_ends(I), y_xx(I), I1 is I + 1, x(I1,J).
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref w-by-2 (list 'c) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list I _) x1) t2)
    (let ([I1 (+ I 1)])
      (for ([x3 (in-list (probe y-xx (list I)))])
        (for ([t5 (in-list (hash-ref x-by-1 (list I1) null))])
          (match-define (cons (list _ J) x4) t5)
          (add! next-y (list I J) (&& x1 (! (holds y-ends (list I))) x3 x4))))))
  ;; y(I,J) :- w(I,c), \+ y_ends(I), \+ y_xx(I), I1 is I + 1, s(I1,J).
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref w-by-2 (list 'c) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list I _) x1) t2)
    (let ([I1 (+ I 1)])
      (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref s-by-1 (list I1) null))])
        (match-define (cons (list _ J) x3) t4)
        (add! next-y (list I J) (&& x1 (! (holds y-ends (list I))) (! (holds y-xx (list I))) x3)))))
  ;; s(I,J) :- s_order(I), x(I,K), y(K,J).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs s-order)])
    (match-define (cons (list I) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref x-by-1 (list I) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ K) x3) t4)
      (for ([t6 (in-list (hash-ref y-by-1 (list K) null))])
        (match-define (cons (list _ J) x5) t6)
        (add! next-s (list I J) (&& x1 x3 x5)))))
  ;; s(I,J) :- \+ s_order(I), y(I,K), x(K,J).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs y)])
    (match-define (cons (list I K) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref x-by-1 (list K) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ J) x3) t4)
      (add! next-s (list I J) (&& x1 (! (holds s-order (list I))) x3))))
  (list next-s next-y))
(define-values (s y)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash) (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-s rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define symbols symbols-facts)

(define generated (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; generated :- symbols(N), s(0,N).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs symbols)])
    (match-define (cons (list N) x1) t2)
    (for ([x3 (in-list (probe s (list 0 N)))])

fix_ = lambda g_, x_: (lambda y_: x_ if y_ == x_ else fix_(g_, y_))(g_(x_))
dedup_ = lambda xs_: list(dict.fromkeys(xs_))
cat_ = lambda ls_: [x_ for l_ in ls_ for x_ in l_]
index_ = lambda ts_: {t_: j_ for j_, t_ in enumerate(ts_)}
by_ = lambda ts_, ps_: reduce(lambda d_, j_: d_.setdefault(tuple(ts_[j_][p_] for p_ in ps_), []).append(j_) or d_,
                              range(len(ts_)), {})
idiv_ = lambda a_, b_: abs(a_) // abs(b_) * (1 if (a_ < 0) == (b_ < 0) else -1)
# the heads of relation q_ that matches ms_ give; a coin's index for each probability below 1
heads_ = lambda q_, ms_: [h_ for m_ in ms_ for r_, h_ in m_[1] if r_ == q_]
coins_of_ = lambda ps_, c0_: [None if p_ >= 1 else c0_ + n_
                              for p_, n_ in zip(ps_, accumulate([0] + [int(x_ < 1) for x_ in ps_]))]
# a relation's instances, each (its tuple's index, its coin and value or None, its refs); their indexes by tuple
facts_ = lambda i_, ts_, cs_: [(i_[t_], None if c_ is None else (c_, 1), []) for t_, c_ in zip(ts_, cs_)]
inst_ = lambda q_, i_, ms_, ks_, c0_: [(i_[h_], None if ks_ is None else (c0_ + ks_[m_[0]], n_ + 1), m_[2])
                                      for m_ in ms_ for n_, (r_, h_) in enumerate(m_[1]) if r_ == q_]
by_tuple_ = lambda es_, n_: (lambda d_: [d_.get((j_,), []) for j_ in range(n_)])(by_(es_, (0,)))
# the tuples (relation, index) that a tuple's instances read; those that tuples us_ read in turn, where ok_
reads_ = lambda u_: ([(r_, k_) for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]] for r_, k_, _, _ in insts_[u_[0]][m_][2]]

reach_ = lambda us_, ok_: fix_(lambda s_: s_ | {w_ for u_ in s_ for w_ in reads_(u_) if ok_(w_)}, frozenset(us_))
# a component's steps, each (relation, instance, stage, cycle), over the tuples of its relations c_ that the
# queries and the evidence read: its cycles of tuples (the tuples that reach the same ones), each after the
# cycles it reads (which reach fewer), in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before
cycles_ = lambda rs_: sorted(reduce(lambda d_, u_: d_.setdefault(rs_[u_], []).append(u_) or d_, sorted(rs_),
                                    {}).values(), key=lambda us_: (len(rs_[us_[0]]), us_[0]))
steps_ = lambda c_: [(u_[0], m_, s_, g_) for g_, us_ in enumerate(cycles_(
                         {u_: reach_([u_], lambda w_: w_[0] in c_) for u_ in used_ if u_[0] in c_}))
                     for s_ in range(1, len(us_) + 1) for u_ in us_ for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]]]
# a step's tuple and stage; the step of a tuple's last instance at each stage; a tuple's last stage and its
# cycle; the step before each, where it is an earlier instance of its tuple at its stage
key_ = lambda x_: (x_[0], insts_[x_[0]][x_[1]][0], x_[2])
at_of_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_): k_ for k_, x_ in enumerate(st_)}
ends_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_)[:2]: (x_[2], x_[3]) for x_ in st_}
prev_ = lambda st_: [k_ - 1 if k_ and key_(st_[k_ - 1]) == key_(st_[k_]) else None for k_ in range(len(st_))]
# events: a fact's; a tuple's at stage s_ (None its last, 0 before the first); a step's coin and body, which
# reads the tuples of its own cycle at the stage before; the step's or the one before it
fact_ = lambda c_, v_: (yes_() if v_ else no_()) if c_ is None else coins_[c_] << {v_}
value_ = lambda a_, at_s_, end_, u_, v_, s_: (lambda t_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if t_ == 0
                                              else a_[at_s_[u_ + (t_,)]] << {v_})(end_[u_][0] if s_ is None else s_)
coin_ = lambda c_: [] if c_ is None else [coins_[c_[0]] << {c_[1]}]
step_ = lambda st_, end_, k_: (lambda q_, m_, s_, g_: all_(coin_(insts_[q_][m_][1]) + [
    at_[r_](j_, v_, s_ - 1 if w_ and end_[(r_, j_)][1] == g_ else None)
    for r_, j_, v_, w_ in insts_[q_][m_][2]]))(*st_[k_])
ev_ = lambda e_, p_, acc_: e_ if p_ is None else e_ | (acc_(p_) << {1})

    for j1, (K, D) in enumerate(demand_4_r)
    if K < D
    for K1 in [(K + 1)]
    for j2 in step_rby_2_3.get((K1, D), [])
    for (I, _, _) in [step_r[j2]]
    for n4 in [[('stops', j3, 0, 0) for j3 in [stops_i.get((I, K))] if j3 is not None]]])(by_(step_r, (1, 2)))

    for j1, (K, D) in enumerate(demand_4_r)
    if K < D
    for K1 in [(K + 1)]]
# rule 9: demand_4(0,D) :- demand_6(Min), at(I,V), V >= Min, D is V - Min.

    for j1, (Min,) in enumerate(demand_6_r)
    for j2, (I, V) in enumerate(at_t)

    for j1, (Min,) in enumerate(demand_6_r)

# S -> XX YY | YY XX
# XX -> aa | bb XX XX 
# YY -> cc | cc XX | cc S

function pcfg_defs()

    Pluck.define_type!(:pcfg_grammar_symbol, Dict(:SS => Symbol[], :XX => Symbol[], :YY => Symbol[], :a => Symbol[], :b => Symbol[], :c => Symbol[]))

    @define "generate_pcfg_grammar" """
    (Y (λ generate symbol -> 
      (case symbol of 
        SS => (let (xgen (generate ( XX )) ygen (generate (YY)) order (flip 0.5))
          (if order (append xgen ygen) (append ygen xgen)))
        XX => (if (flip 0.5) (Cons (a) (Nil)) (Cons (b) (append (generate (XX)) (generate (XX)))))
        YY => (Cons (c) (if (flip 0.5) (Nil) (generate (if (flip 0.5) (XX) (SS)))))
      )
    ))
    """

    @define "generate_pcfg_grammar_fuel" """
    (Y (λ generate fuel symbol -> 
      (case fuel of
        S fuel => 
          (case symbol of 
            SS => (let (xgen (generate fuel ( XX )) ygen (generate fuel (YY)) order (flip 0.5))
                (if order (append xgen ygen) (append ygen xgen)))
            XX => (if (flip 0.5) (Cons (a) (Nil)) (Cons (b) (append (generate fuel (XX)) (generate fuel (XX)))))
            YY => (Cons (c) (if (flip 0.5) (Nil) (generate fuel (if (flip 0.5) (XX) (SS)))))
          )
      )
    ))
    """

    @define "symbol_equals" """
    (λ symbol1 symbol2 ->
      (case symbol1 of
        a => (case symbol2 of
          a => true
          b => false
          c => false)
        b => (case symbol2 of
          a => false
          b => true
          c => false)
        c => (case symbol2 of
          a => false
          b => false
          c => true)
      )
    )
    """

    @define "list_symbols_equal" """
    (Y (λ rec list1 list2 ->
      (case list1 of
        Nil => (case list2 of
          Nil => true
          Cons _ _ => false)
        Cons hd1 tl1 => (case list2 of
          Nil => false
          Cons hd2 tl2 => (and (symbol_equals hd1 hd2) (rec tl1 tl2)))
      )
    ))
    """
end

function make_string_from_julia_list(l)
    # l is a list of symbols :a, :b, :c
    # We want to return a string that looks like (Cons (a) (Cons (b) (Cons (c) (Nil))))
    result = ""
    for symbol in l
        result *= "(Cons ($symbol) "
    end
    result *= "(Nil)" * repeat(")", length(l))
    return result
end

# test_example_string = [:c, :c, :b, :a, :b, :b, :a, :b, :a, :a, :b, :b, :a, :a, :a, :a, :a]
test_example_string = [:c, :b, :b, :b, :a, :b, :b, :a, :b, :a, :b, :b, :a, :b, :a, :a, :a, :a, :a, :b, :a, :a, :a]
test_example_string_program = make_string_from_julia_list(test_example_string)


pcfg_query() = "(list_symbols_equal (generate_pcfg_grammar (SS)) $test_example_string_program)"


pcfg_example_enum() = lazy_enumerate("(list_symbols_equal (generate_pcfg_grammar (SS)) $test_example_string_program)"; disable_cache = true)

function make_long_observation_string(n)
    result_prefix = ""
    result_suffix = ""
    # something of the form abababababab...bcbcbcbcbc with a c in the middle
    for i = 1:n
        result_prefix *= "(Cons (a) (Cons (b) "
        result_suffix *= "(Cons (b) (Cons (c) "
    end
    result_suffix *= "(Nil)" * repeat(")", 4n + 1)
    return result_prefix * "(Cons (c) " * result_suffix
end


pcfg_example_long(n) = "(list_symbols_equal (generate_dice_grammar (Start)) $(make_long_observation_string(n)))"
pcfg_example_long_fuel(n, fuel) = "(list_symbols_equal (generate_dice_grammar_fuel $fuel (Start)) $(make_long_observation_string(n)))"

function run_pcfg_bdd()
    pcfg_defs()
    @bbtime bdd_forward(pcfg_example_long(20))
end

function run_pcfg_lazy(; fuel = nothing, kwargs...)
    pcfg_defs()
    if isnothing(fuel)
        @bbtime lazy_enumerate(pcfg_example_long(20); $kwargs...)
    else
        @bbtime lazy_enumerate(pcfg_example_long_fuel(20, $fuel); $kwargs...)
    end
end

;; pluck_sorted_list.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define at-facts (hash-ref db "at/2" (make-hash)))
(define elements-facts (hash-ref db "elements/1" (make-hash)))

(define at at-facts)

(define stops (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.5::stops(I,K) :- at(I,V), between(0,V,K).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs at)])
    (match-define (cons (list I V) x1) t2)
    (for ([K (in-range 0 (+ V 1))])
      (add! stops (list I K) (&& x1 (flip 0.5))))))

;; demand_4/2, demand_6/1, step/3: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define (stage-demand-4 demand-4 demand-6 step)
  (define next-demand-4 (make-hash))
  (define next-demand-6 (make-hash))
  (define next-step (make-hash))
  (define step-by-2-3 (index step 1 2))
  ;; step(I,D,D) :- stops(I,D).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs stops)])
    (match-define (cons (list I D) x1) t2)
    (add! next-step (list I D D) x1))
  ;; step(I,K,D) :- demand_4(K,D), K < D, \+ stops(I,K), K1 is K + 1, step(I,K1,D).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs demand-4)])
    (match-define (cons (list K D) x1) t2)
    (when (< K D)
      (let ([K1 (+ K 1)])
        (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref step-by-2-3 (list K1 D) null))])
          (match-define (cons (list I _ _) x3) t4)
          (add! next-step (list I K D) (&& x1 x3 (! (holds stops (list I K)))))))))
  ;; demand_4(K1,D) :- demand_4(K,D), K < D, K1 is K + 1.
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs demand-4)])
    (match-define (cons (list K D) x1) t2)
    (when (< K D)
      (let ([K1 (+ K 1)])
        (add! next-demand-4 (list K1 D) #t))))
  ;; demand_4(0,D) :- demand_6(Min), at(I,V), V >= Min, D is V - Min.
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs demand-6)])
    (match-define (cons (list Min) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-hash-pairs at)])
      (match-define (cons (list I V) x3) t4)
      (when (>= V Min)
        (let ([D (- V Min)])
          (add! next-demand-4 (list 0 D) #t)))))
  ;; demand_6(V) :- demand_6(Min), at(I,V), V >= Min, D is V - Min, step(I,0,D), I1 is I + 1.
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs demand-6)])
    (match-define (cons (list Min) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-hash-pairs at)])
      (match-define (cons (list I V) x3) t4)
      (when (>= V Min)
        (let ([D (- V Min)])
          (let ([I1 (+ I 1)])
            (for ([x5 (in-list (probe step (list I 0 D)))])
              (add! next-demand-6 (list V) #t)))))))
  ;; demand_6(0).
  (add! next-demand-6 (list 0) #t)
  (list next-demand-4 next-demand-6 next-step))
(define-values (demand-4 demand-6 step)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash) (make-hash) (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-demand-4 rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define demand-5 (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; demand_5(V) :- demand_6(Min), at(I,V), V >= Min, D is V - Min, step(I,0,D), I1 is I + 1.
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs demand-6)])
    (match-define (cons (list Min) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-hash-pairs at)])
      (match-define (cons (list I V) x3) t4)
      (when (>= V Min)
        (let ([D (- V Min)])
          (let ([I1 (+ I 1)])
            (for ([x5 (in-list (probe step (list I 0 D)))])
              (add! demand-5 (list V) #t)))))))
  ;; demand_5(0).
  (add! demand-5 (list 0) #t))

(define elements elements-facts)

(define ends (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.5::ends(I) :- elements(N), between(0,N,I).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs elements)])
    (match-define (cons (list N) x1) t2)
    (for ([I (in-range 0 (+ N 1))])
      (add! ends (list I) (&& x1 (flip 0.5))))))

;; list/2: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define (stage-list- list-)
  (define next-list- (make-hash))
  ;; list(N,Anon1) :- demand_5(Anon1), elements(N), ends(N).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs demand-5)])
    (match-define (cons (list Anon1) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-hash-pairs elements)])
      (match-define (cons (list N) x3) t4)
      (for ([x5 (in-list (probe ends (list N)))])
        (add! next-list- (list N Anon1) (&& x1 x3 x5)))))
  ;; list(I,Min) :- demand_6(Min), at(I,V), \+ ends(I), V >= Min, D is V - Min, step(I,0,D), I1 is I + 1, list(I1,V).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs demand-6)])
    (match-define (cons (list Min) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-hash-pairs at)])
      (match-define (cons (list I V) x3) t4)
      (when (>= V Min)
        (let ([D (- V Min)])
          (let ([I1 (+ I 1)])
            (for ([x5 (in-list (probe step (list I 0 D)))])
              (for ([x6 (in-list (probe list- (list I1 V)))])
                (add! next-list- (list I Min) (&& x1 x3 (! (holds ends (list I))) x5 x6)))))))))
  (list next-list-))
(define-values (list-)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-list- rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define generated (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; generated :- list(0,0).
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe list- (list 0 0)))])
    (add! generated (list) x1)))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds generated (list)))))
(statement (report dists))

% string_editing: ported to ProbLog from PluckArtifact.jl/src/table1/
% sequence_models/pluck/string_editing.jl of the artifact of Bowers, Lew,
% Tenenbaum, Solar-Lezama and Mansinghka, "Stochastic Lazy Knowledge
% Compilation for Inference in Discrete Probabilistic Programs" (PLDI
% 2025), Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15051140 (CC-BY-4.0): the Pluck program of
% the paper's Table 1, row String Editing, with the perturb its benchmark
% defines (perturb_defs, "the one we're using"). The query is the
% probability that perturb turns "edcc" into "eddde":
%   perturb Nil         = random_string 0.99
%   perturb (Cons c cs) = let delete = flip 0.01, insertion = random_string 0.99,
%                             rest = perturb cs
%                         in if delete then rest
%                            else insertion ++ Cons (if flip 0.01 then random_char else c) rest
%   random_string p     = if flip p then Nil else Cons random_char (random_string p)
% with random_char uniform over a to e.

% The perturbation is read against the target left to right: pert(K, I)
% holds where perturb of the input from position K = the target from
% position I to its end, and ins(K, I, J) where the string inserted before
% input position K (K = 4: after the input) is the target's symbols I to
% J - 1. A choice is keyed by the input position it perturbs and, within
% an inserted string, by the target position it writes, which gives the
% original's distribution where no perturbation reads one key twice. The
% input positions are perturbed once each, in order, and an inserted
% string writes each target position once, its end read at the position
% after its last symbol; an empty insertion, or a deleted input
% character, leaves the target position to the next input position, a
% key of its own. No perturbation then reads one key twice, it has the
% original's probability, and the choices at its keys fix it, so that two
% perturbations exclude each other.
in(0, e). in(1, d). in(2, c). in(3, c).
input(4).
out(0, e). out(1, d). out(2, d). out(3, d). out(4, e).
target(5).
place(K) :- input(N), between(0, N, K).

0.01::deleted(K) :- in(K, V1).
0.01::replaced(K) :- in(K, V2).
0.2::replacement(K, a); 0.2::replacement(K, b); 0.2::replacement(K, c);
  0.2::replacement(K, d); 0.2::replacement(K, e) :- in(K, V3).
0.99::ends(K, I) :- place(K), target(M), between(0, M, I).
0.2::inserted(K, I, a); 0.2::inserted(K, I, b); 0.2::inserted(K, I, c);
  0.2::inserted(K, I, d); 0.2::inserted(K, I, e) :- place(K), out(I, V4).

ins(K, I, I) :- ends(K, I).
ins(K, I, J) :- out(I, C), \+ends(K, I), inserted(K, I, C), I1 = I + 1, ins(K, I1, J).
written(K, C, C) :- in(K, C), \+replaced(K).
written(K, C, D) :- in(K, C), replaced(K), replacement(K, D).
pert(N, I) :- input(N), target(M), ins(N, I, M).
pert(K, I) :- in(K, V5), deleted(K), K1 = K + 1, pert(K1, I).
pert(K, I) :- in(K, C), \+deleted(K), ins(K, I, J), out(J, D), written(K, C, D),
  J1 = J + 1, K1 = K + 1, pert(K1, J1).

perturbed :- pert(0, 0).
query(perturbed).
